name: scene3d_patch_objects
description: Batch-patch existing scene objects. Each item is {id, patch:{...}} — put the changed fields inside `patch`, never on the item. Errors on missing id — re-read with scene3d_state, never recreate. Patch fields: transform (rotationY deg; scale, or scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ to squash one axis), color, placedInScene, visible, label, pose (person stance), dimensions {width,height,depth} (resize to a size in world units — scene3d_state reports it as `dim`), primitiveDimensions, parts (compound object), forwardAxis (positiveZ/negativeZ), groupId (clusters into a frontend group; same id = same group). Resizing routes by what the object is made of: a primitive takes the literal dimensions, a compound (parts) object is scaled per axis so its parts keep their proportions, and an asset/GLB object is refused with realSizeM named instead — a size patch is never reported as applied when it would not change the rendered object. faceToward {x,z} re-aims rotationY using the stored or patched forwardAxis. realSizeM re-sizes an asset object to a real-world length in meters. Every item is applied independently: the response lists `patched`, `reanchored` and `failed`, so read it instead of assuming the whole batch landed. Repositioning an actor that already holds a generated performance IS allowed — its route travels with it and the performance is kept. Turning one (transform.rotationY or faceToward) is allowed too when its performance happens in place; when that performance walks a route, the facing is refused while the move still lands. Rescaling or re-posing a performing actor still needs scene3d_remove_actor_motion first. The failed reason always says what landed, and `reoriented` lists the actors whose facing changed. @see guides_get('scene3d')

patches.description: Batch all edits in ONE call. Shape: [{ "id": "agent-…", "patch": { "color": "#ff00ff" } }].

id.description: Existing object id (from scene3d_state/scene3d_add_objects). Just the id — do NOT append the patch here.

patch.description: Changed fields ONLY, nested here: transform (rotationY deg; y = object BASE, not center; scale or scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ), color, placedInScene, visible, label, dimensions {width,height,depth} in world units (resize: literal for a primitive, per-axis scale for a compound object), primitiveDimensions, parts, forwardAxis (positiveZ/negativeZ), groupId, faceToward {x,z}, realSizeM (meters, longest axis, overrides transform.scale — asset objects only), pose (person stance: Relaxed | Walking | Running | Sitting | Crouching | Kneeling | Jumping | Kick | Celebration | Dance).
